tasks.title: backoff_delay(): exponential backoff with a hard cap
tasks.description: Implement backoff_delay(int $attempt): int, which returns how many seconds to wait before retry attempt $attempt (1-based: attempt 1 is the first retry). The delay doubles with every attempt, starting at 2 seconds, and must never exceed the 3600-second cap. Examples: backoff_delay(1) returns 2, backoff_delay(10) returns 1024, backoff_delay(12) returns 3600 (2**12 = 4096 is capped).

tasks.title: should_retry(): off-by-one grants a job one attempt too many
tasks.description: A job may run at most $maxAttempts times in total. Given how many times it has already run ($attempt, 1-based), should_retry(int $attempt, int $maxAttempts): bool must return true only while budget remains for another run. Hint: the boundary comparison is off by one — when the current attempt equals the maximum, the job must NOT be retried, but the <= comparison schedules one extra attempt beyond the budget. Examples: should_retry(2, 3) returns true, should_retry(3, 3) returns false, should_retry(1, 1) returns false.

tasks.title: Design failed-job handling for a Laravel queue consumer
tasks.description: A webhook job in a Laravel app calls a third-party billing API that intermittently returns 5xx, and occasionally receives a permanently malformed payload. Right now a failure kills the job silently and nothing is logged or retried. Design the failed-job handling end to end: the retry strategy on the job class, how you treat transient vs permanent failures, idempotency of the side effect, what happens after the last retry (failed_jobs table, failed() hook), and how you protect workers from poison pills.
tasks.solution:
Start from delivery semantics: Laravel queues give at-least-once delivery — a worker can crash after popping a job but before its side effect commits, so a job may run more than once. Exactly-once is not achievable in a distributed system, so the design builds an idempotent consumer first and layers retry policy on top.

On the job class, replace the defaults with an explicit strategy: a retry cap such as public $tries = 5, or better a retryUntil set to now()->addMinutes(30) when retries must stop at a wall-clock deadline, plus a backoff() returning an exponential sequence like [5, 15, 60, 300] so transient outages do not hammer the endpoint. Classify failures: a permanently malformed payload will never succeed, so catch it and call $this->fail() to send the job straight to failed_jobs instead of burning retries; let 5xx responses and timeouts bubble up as retryable.

Make the side effect idempotent so duplicates are harmless: persist the external event/order identifier and back it with a unique DB constraint, or record processed ids, so a re-delivered job becomes a no-op.

When tries are exhausted the job lands in the failed_jobs table. Implement the failed(Throwable $e) hook (or a Queue::failing listener) to log the payload, page on-call, and copy it to a dead-letter store for replay; operators can inspect and requeue entries with php artisan queue:failed and queue:retry.

A poison-pill job that always fails is bounded by tries and ends in failed_jobs, so it cannot stall a healthy worker. The subtler risks are jobs that never finish: give every job a timeout, monitor queue depth and latency with Horizon, and drain workers with --stop-when-empty or --max-time during deploys so in-flight work completes before code changes underneath it.

criteria: States that queue delivery is at-least-once, so consumers must be idempotent, and explains why exactly-once is not achievable.
Configures tries/retryUntil and a capped, exponential backoff() instead of relying on queue defaults.
Separates permanent from transient failures: permanent errors fast-fail via $this->fail(), transient ones retry.
Designs idempotency (persisted external id backed by a unique constraint or processed-id record).
Defines the failed()/Queue::failing hook with alerting and a dead-letter path, plus queue:failed/queue:retry for replay.
Handles poison pills via retry bounds, per-job timeouts, Horizon monitoring, and worker draining during deploys.
key_points: At-least-once: duplicates happen by design; exactly-once is not achievable in distributed systems.
retryUntil time-boxes retries; exponential backoff with a cap backs off gracefully.
Permanent errors fail fast via $this->fail(); transient errors are retried.
failed_jobs table plus the failed() hook provide logging, alerting, and dead-letter replay.
php artisan queue:failed / queue:retry let operators inspect and requeue dead jobs.
Poison pills are bounded by tries; guard against never-finishing jobs with timeouts and Horizon monitoring.
Drain workers on deploy (--stop-when-empty / --max-time) so in-flight work finishes cleanly.
